A plateau's edge at sunset, the land dropping away in vast terraced cliffs behind the battle, the sky ahead blazing orange and purple, two exhausted armies still struggling in the fading light, their long shadows stretching across the bloodied stone.

Before the towering walls of a great besieged castle, siege-towers grinding forward, ladders against the ramparts, the battle spilling across the field below in churned earth and smoke rising to a leaden sky.
A vast open plain stretching to a hazy horizon under a brooding storm-sky, the two armies' lines running away to either side, churned mud and trampled grass beneath a ceiling of bruised clouds.
A narrow mountain pass choked wall-to-wall with struggling fighters, sheer cliffs rising on both sides, the press of bodies receding into shadow and dust toward a distant sliver of pale sky.

The burning streets of a sacked city, fire leaping between rooftops, smoke columns rising into a red-stained night, fighters clashing amid rubble and fallen timbers as whole districts glow behind them.

A muddy river-crossing at desperate low water, men and horses struggling through brown churning currents, the near and far banks packed with screaming combatants, a broken bridge trailing timbers downstream.

A snow-covered field of war, the white ground stained red in spreading patches, breath-mist rising above the armies, frozen banners hanging still in a bitter grey silence stretching to pale treelines.

The breached gate of a great fortress, the shattered portcullis hanging twisted overhead, the archway packed with fighting men, rubble heaped across the passage, defenders pouring from the walls above.
A broad hilltop and its long slopes, defenders holding the crest against waves of attackers surging upward, the valley far below filled with reserves and standards moving like slow rivers of iron.
An ash-strewn volcanic plain under a sullen orange sky, rivers of old cooled lava cutting the ground, geysers of steam venting from cracks, two armies locked together across the grey desolation.
A misty moor stretching to invisible horizons, heather and bog underfoot, half the battle lost in rolling grey fog, only the clash of steel and the shapes of warriors emerging from the murk.
The vast courtyard of a great keep, high stone walls enclosing the carnage on all sides, towers packed with archers above, the cobbled ground slick with blood, a battle within a battle.
A desert battlefield of dust and dunes, sand devils twisting between the lines, the sun a white disc above bleached emptiness, cavalry sweeping across crests trailing great plumes of ochre dust.
At the foot of a great cliff-face, the battle pressed hard against the rock, no retreat possible, the fighting dense and savage, ravens circling the top of the stone wall far above.
A frozen lake battlefield, ice groaning underfoot, cracks spidering outward from the press of men and horses, the far shore dim through blowing snow, the sky and ice the same pale grey.
A dense ancient forest clearing, the trees pressing close on all sides, roots and undergrowth tripping the fighters, shafts of weak light cutting through the canopy above a mass of struggling men.

The rubble-strewn ruins of a fallen city, broken columns and toppled arches providing cover, the battle threading through roofless halls and collapsed streets, dust hanging over everything like a second sky.
A coastal headland battered by sea-wind, the cliff edge at one flank with waves crashing far below, the battle surging back and forth across short salt-grass under a hard grey Atlantic sky.

A wide shallow valley between two ridgelines, both heights bristling with archers and artillery, the valley floor choked with infantry locked together, the slopes dark with watching reserves waiting their moment.

A swamp battlefield of black water and reed-islands, fighters moving on narrow causeways between the mires, cavalry useless, the ground swallowing the fallen, fog drifting low across the brown water between the islands.
Before the pylons of a great bridge over a gorge, the bridge itself the only crossing, the near side a heaving mass of attackers, the gorge falling away to white water far below.
A high alpine meadow ringed by snowpeaks, the air thin and cold, the grass vivid green against the white summits, two armies filling the bowl of the valley, their noise rising to the silence above.
A sunbaked steppe under a merciless midday sun, the land flat and featureless to every horizon, dust rising from thousands of marching feet, the sky enormous and blank above the locked armies below.
The terraced hillside of an abandoned vineyard, stone walls cutting the slopes into levels, men fighting tier by tier, the town far below in the valley, smoke rising from its rooftops.

A tidal estuary at low water, the mud flats exposed, fighters slipping and sinking, the flanks anchored on shingle banks, the tide beginning to return along the distant channels toward the struggling mass.
The outer ward of a concentric castle, inner walls rising behind the defenders, the outer wall already lost, the fighting compressed into a killing ground of stone, the sky a narrow strip above.

Before the towering walls of a great besieged castle, battering rams and siege-towers grinding forward, ladders swarming the ramparts, smoke and screaming banners filling the air above a field churned to ruin.
